title: access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics acceptance[4]/[6]: re-point the audit clause to ADR-0131 D7/D9 (sys_audit_log is off the wall; tenant_id is attribution)
body:
qa#2 · os-bob · session_012dn2Acf5wtyrf2yKWCThBj

QA-source: #32102 · access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics · acceptance[4]

Stale-spec re-point card (checklist-test §5) for a checklist item in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json`.

## What the run measured

QA run #32102, subject `ff04ad81`, on walled group and isolated boots with producer (2) of knownGaps[0]:

- A member clears its active organization and then signs out. The logout row carries `tenant_id` NULL.
- The operator can read that row (200). The member gets 403 (object permission).
- Repro rule R-1 in the record.

## Governing text

- ADR-0131 D7: `sys_audit_log` is "governed by object permission, not by the wall".
- D7's note of 2026-10-22: "`sys_audit_log.tenant_id` keeps its NULL arm, by design … it is not a tenant column".
- D9: column ⇒ in scope.

The clause and its "invisible to RLS readers" premise predate D7 (#8245, from when the ledger was walled).

## Re-point

- acceptance[4] (clause and verify): replace "no audit row is NULL-tenanted … invisible to RLS readers" with the D7 reading, which states who must be able to read the row.
- acceptance[6]: state that the audit ledger's NULL attribution is not a disagreement under D7.
- knownGaps[3]: extend the open question to producer (2).
- Drop the item's `blocked` marker (#9334). The walled boot ran from the tree with the three variables and served every leg.
- Drop knownGaps[4] and knownGaps[5]: #24784 holds live on group.

## Question for the maintainer, carried here

Should a logout by an org member who cleared its active organization carry organization attribution? If the answer is "must be attributed", this becomes a product defect in plugin-auth `auth-session-audit.ts` `logoutEventFor`, which takes the session's `activeOrganizationId`.
